# Contributing Guidelines

Thank you for considering contributing to this project. Contributions of all sizes are welcome and appreciated.

## Getting Started

### 1. Fork the Repository

Create a fork of this repository under your GitHub account.

### 2. Create a New Branch

Create a descriptive branch for your changes:

```bash
git checkout -b feature/my-feature
```

### 3. Make Your Changes

Implement your feature, bug fix, documentation update, or improvement.

### 4. Commit Your Changes

Use clear and descriptive commit messages:

```bash
git commit -m "Add dark mode support"
```

### 5. Push Your Branch

```bash
git push origin feature/my-feature
```

### 6. Open a Pull Request

Submit a Pull Request with a detailed description of your changes.

---

## Contribution Standards

### Code Quality

Please ensure that your contribution:

- Follows the existing project structure.
- Uses clear and maintainable code.
- Removes unused code and assets.
- Does not introduce unnecessary dependencies.
- Preserves existing functionality.

### Documentation

If your contribution changes functionality, usage, or behavior, update the relevant documentation accordingly.

---

## Commit Message Guidelines

Use concise and meaningful commit messages.

### Good Examples

```text
Fix navbar responsiveness
Add dark mode support
Improve accessibility for forms
Update README examples
Refactor authentication logic
```

### Avoid

```text
update
fix stuff
changes
misc fixes
final update
```

---

## Reporting Issues

Before opening an issue:

- Search existing issues to avoid duplicates.
- Provide clear reproduction steps.
- Include screenshots or logs when applicable.
- Describe expected and actual behavior.

---

## Pull Request Checklist

Before submitting a Pull Request, verify that:

- [ ] Your code builds successfully.
- [ ] Existing functionality remains intact.
- [ ] Documentation has been updated when necessary.
- [ ] Changes are limited to the scope of the issue.
- [ ] Commit messages follow the project guidelines.

---

## Need Help?

If you have questions, need clarification, or would like feedback before starting work, feel free to open an issue or start a discussion.

Thank you for helping improve this project.
